description.narrative: In April 2021, the Federal Technical and Vocational Education and Training Agency (FTVETA), in collaboration with social partners, reviewed and validated the Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) policy and framework. The RPL policy applied ILO tools (ILO RPL learning package of 2018) and standards in its formulation. As a result, RPL is now recognised as an integral part of the broader skills development strategy in Ethiopia as indicated in the new TVET policy and strategy. The ILO supported FTVETA in developing the RPL policy framework, including the implementation guidelines and tools. The ILO facilitated consultation with national partners during the drafting stage of the document. Finally, the ILO undertook the review of the final document to ensure its alignment with ILO tools and guidelines.

title.narrative: 5.3.3. Number of member States with inclusive skills recognition mechanisms
Output 5.1. Increased capacity of the ILO constituents to identify current skills mismatches and anticipate future skill needs

description.narrative:
In February 2020, the Federal Technical and Vocational Education and Training Agency (FTVETA) reviewed and validated occupational standards for the textile sector. Six occupational profiles were developed and an assessment tool was prepared and implemented in March 2021.
As an input the ongoing national strategic 10-year planning initiative, the Job Creation Commission has undertaken the skills planning exercise across three sectors, based on the ILO's sectoral approach to skills anticipation (STED). Through the Norway funded Global Programme on Skills and Lifelong Learning (GPSL3), the ILO provided support in capacity development on skills needs anticipation and matching for stakeholders including the Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs (MoLSA), Jobs Creation Commission (JCC), Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET), Confederation of Ethiopian Employers' Federation (CEEF), Confederation of Ethiopian Trade Unions (CETU) and others, as well as on the development of the occupational standards and assessment tool. In addition, the ILO through the Netherlands funded PROSPECTS project supported four experts (PROSPECTS partners) for the above mentioned capacity development on skills needs anticipation and matching in May 2021. The training focused on different tools and methods to overcome and prevent skills mismatches. Case studies from other countries were presented using Skills for Trade and Economic Diversification (STED). This training will continue to be provided to different organisations in the future both online and face-to-face.
The ILO Rapid assessment of reskilling and upskilling needs in the context of the COVID-19 was conducted in two sectors jointly agreed and implemented with JCC (agro-processing and tourism and hospitality).
The four PROSPECTS partners, which represented the Somali regional state TVET Bureau, Agency of Competence, Bureau of Labour, and Jigjiga Polytechnic College, submitted a joint action plan around assessing the local labour market, for further discussion with the ILO.
The assessment on "Youth employment opportunities in the digital economy in Ethiopia: Afar and Somali regions", in April 2021, under the ILO-PROSPECTS project, was funded by the Netherlands government and with the technical backstopping of the ILO and the ITU. The study may give additional insights in the skills development needs of the digital sector.

title.narrative: 5.1.1. Number of member States that have applied ILO approaches to measure skills mismatches and/or anticipate future skill needs at national and/or sectoral level
Output 5.3. Increased capacity of the ILO constituents to design and deliver innovative, flexible and inclusive learning options, encompassing work-based learning and quality apprenticeships

description.narrative:
In July 2021, Somali Regional Government endorsed the establishment of an inclusive vocational centre and the development of inclusive skills programmes in Kebrebeya Woreda for the inclusion of host and refugee community. As a result: - A memorandum of understanding (MoU) has been approved for signature by relevant regional Bureaus. The MoU articulates the commitment and roles by the regional government departments to expand access to, and design inclusive and flexible on demand skills programmes targeting women and youth from the refugees and host community The Local Government Authority established a steering committee that has guided the design of inclusive, flexible and on-demand skills programmes targeting women, refugees and members of the host communities. Through social dialogue and advise, the Local Committee is guiding and contributing to the design and implementation of skills and livelihood programmes. To demonstrate their commitment and support, the Mayor of the Kebrebeya Town has donated several buildings and land for the rehabilitation and construction of the vocational Centre.
In May 2021, 11 participants from local and international NGOs, UN partners and public and private institutions in Somali region, received training of trainers on "social cohesion in fragile contexts through TVET". As a result, the participating organizations developed action plans to apply the social cohesion tool in their programmes and interventions. By August 2021, 6 out of the 11 participants reported that they have successfully integrated social cohesion tool into their training and programmes. Through the support of the Government of the Netherlands, the ILO facilitated the consultations with key regional and local government stakeholders to identify and agree on priority occupations. The ILO also conducted a TVET capacity gaps assessment and market analysis to identify skills development needs, market dynamics and demand that has informed the design and development of the inclusive skills programmes. In addition, the ILO consulted and established an implementation partnership with Lutheran world Federation (INGO) with local presence and experience at the Somali region. The two partners, with regional government leadership have supported the local authority and stakeholders to design of an inclusive and tailored skills development centre and programmes.
The design of the centre has applied ILO's principals on inclusion for people with disability, the use of EIIP principle and approach in the construction and rehabilitation work.
The ILO developed a guide on Promoting Social Cohesion and Peaceful Coexistence in Fragile Contexts through TVET and facilitated its piloting in 3 countries in Africa including Ethiopia. This tool contributes to the implementation of ILO Recommendation No. 205. In Ethiopia, the local and national partners have found the tool relevant in fragile conditions such as in refugee context and have already started adopting the methodology.

title.narrative: 5.3.2. Number of member States with innovative, flexible and inclusive skills programmes and services targeting women, youth or persons in vulnerable situations
Output 5.2. Increased capacity of member States to strengthen skills and lifelong learning policies, governance models and financing system

description.narrative: In consultation with government and other key stakeholders, the lead associations in the garment and textiles and agro processing sectors established two sector skills councils in March 2020. This industry initiative was in response to the implementation of the educational sector roadmap (2018 – 2030). The sector skills councils reflect a new approach to skills governance in Ethiopia. They have undertaken detailed sectoral analysis and have initiated various activities to improve training relevance at sectoral level. With the joint support from the government of Norway and European Union, the ILO convened consultative meetings that led to the establishment of sector skills council and provided initial support as they commenced operations. The ILO also developed operational guidelines and resource mobilization strategies for the established sector skills councils.
